m1-server-core.title: scripts/mcp_spine_server.py: zero-dep JSON-RPC server, full 7-tool surface, wraps main() only
m1-server-core.imperative: Build scripts/mcp_spine_server.py: newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio, zero dependencies, binding SPINE_FILE/SPINE_ENGINE/SPINE_SESSION from the environment (never tool args). Every tool builds an argv and calls checklist_engine.main(argv), capturing stdout/stderr/exit code -- never reimplements engine logic. Implement all 7 tools now (spine_status=current; spine_lease=claim|release|heartbeat; spine_start=start; spine_advance=advance; spine_evidence=attest|attach|waive; spine_halt=block|resume; spine_survey_result=record|consolidate) plus initialize and tools/list. A refusal (exit!=0) must map to isError:true carrying the engine's stdout+stderr verbatim (its own refusal text + recovery hint), never reworded. Prove the door is genuinely up BEFORE anything else: drive raw JSON-RPC (initialize, tools/list, one real spine_status call against a throwaway spine) and capture the server's actual reply showing genuine engine output -- this is DC3's positive control and it must exist before any later no-identity result counts. Attach the CLI-fallback table (verbs NOT covered: skip, reopen, append, amend, flag-candidate, and why) to the module docstring.

m2-drive-to-done.title: Prove the full tool surface: drive a throwaway spine to DONE, prove refusal->isError, prove byte-identical imperative text
m2-drive-to-done.imperative: Build a throwaway scratch gated spine (mixed condition kinds: command-checked and attested postconditions, at least one waivable postcondition with override_policy.allowed=true, and one gate needing attach for a user-decision-shaped artifact) under crew-plans/scratch-mcp/. Write a raw-JSON-RPC driver (no model in the loop) that speaks to the server over stdio and drives the spine through claim -> start -> attest/attach -> advance ... to DONE, exercising every one of the 7 tools at least once (spine_status, spine_lease claim+release, spine_start, spine_advance, spine_evidence attest+attach+waive, spine_halt block+resume, spine_survey_result on a small survey fixture). Separately prove refusal shape: attempt an illegal advance (unmet postcondition) through spine_advance and assert the tool result has isError:true and its text contains the engine's own REFUSED/recovery text verbatim. Separately prove byte-identity: for the same spine state, capture `python scripts/checklist_engine.py --file <spine> current` stdout and the spine_status tool result text, and assert they are byte-identical (say how the check could fail: mutate the server to add a leading space and show the assertion catches it).

why_trail.why: Handoff is complete. Design decision made: 7 tools (spine_status=current; spine_lease=claim/release/heartbeat; spine_start=start; spine_advance=advance; spine_evidence=attest/attach/waive; spine_halt=block/resume; spine_survey_result=record/consolidate) covering 13/18 verbs, deliberately including attach+waive per handoff's explicit load-bearing guidance; skip/reopen/append/amend/flag-candidate go to the CLI-fallback table. Server wraps main() only, per prototype's proven shape (env-bound SPINE_FILE/ENGINE/SESSION, argv-build, capture stdout+stderr+code, isError=code!=0).

Server built: 7 tools (spine_status/lease/start/advance/evidence/halt/survey_result), zero deps, wraps main() only via run_engine(), refusals map to isError via as_result (code!=0). CLI-fallback table for skip/reopen/append/amend/flag-candidate lives in the module docstring. Smoke test proves DC3's positive control: initialize returns serverInfo, tools/list returns exactly the 7 committed tools, and a real spine_status call against a fresh scratch spine returns genuine engine 'current' output (ACTIVE g1, the real imperative text, real postcondition ids, real next-verb hint) -- not a stub.

Full tool surface driven end to end through the MCP tools alone: scratch spine reached DONE (with WAIVED g3.c1 recorded), all 7 tools exercised (status/lease-claim-release/start/advance/evidence-attest-attach-waive/halt-block-resume/survey_result-record-consolidate), 18/18 assertions passed 0 failed. Refusal proven: premature advance g1 returned isError:true carrying the engine's literal REFUSED + Recovery: text verbatim. Byte-identity proven: spine_status text == CLI current stdout exactly, AND a mutated copy of the CLI text was shown NOT equal, proving the assertion can fail. Transcript at crew-plans/scratch-mcp/drive_via_mcp.transcript.

gen_mcp_config.py built: emits {mcpServers: {<name>: {command, args:[server], env:{SPINE_FILE,SPINE_ENGINE,SPINE_SESSION=session_id#agent_id}}}}. Proved for real, not by inspection: a headless 'claude -p ... --mcp-config <generated> --strict-mcp-config --allowedTools mcp__spine__spine_status' dispatch against a fresh scratch spine whose g1 imperative carried an unguessable per-run nonce. The dispatch's final answer contained the exact nonce and the real engine current() output verbatim (RAIL line, ACTIVE g1, real postcondition ids, next-verb hint) -- a model cannot guess a random 16-hex-char nonce, so this proves the tool call round-tripped through the generated per-dispatch server and back. Corroborated by the server's own mcp_calls.jsonl logging a real 'current' engine call with matching stdout. Transcript at crew-plans/scratch-mcp/prove_headless_dispatch.transcript.

Wrote .mcp.json at worktree root, project scope, relative paths (command python3, args scripts/mcp_spine_server.py; env SPINE_FILE/SPINE_ENGINE relative, SPINE_SESSION empty so it works session-less, matching the engine's no-lease legacy behavior) so it is portable, not machine-pinned like a generated per-dispatch config. Points at a small throwaway interactive-demo spine (crew-plans/scratch-mcp/interactive-demo/, with its own README) rather than any live project spine, so opening this worktree interactively cannot mutate real run state through the door. Verified relative-path resolution works when the server is launched with cwd=repo root (Claude Code's project-scope convention), by spawning it directly with relative env values and getting genuine engine output back. CLI-fallback table for skip/reopen/append/amend/flag-candidate is in the server module's docstring with exact invocation shape + one-line rationale each; verified all 5 verb names present.

tests/test_mcp_spine_server.py written: 24 tests covering protocol shape (initialize/tools-list exactly 7 tools), every tool genuinely wrapping the engine (verified against real fixture spines, not mocks), refusal->isError with engine text verbatim (cross-checked against the identical CLI call, same session id), byte-identity of spine_status vs CLI current (plus a negative control proving the check can fail), waive satisfying without the underlying check ever becoming true, gen_mcp_config.py's session_id#agentId keying, its generated config launching a real server that answers a real tool call, and .mcp.json's portability + CLI-fallback table completeness. Found and fixed a real bug while writing these: an eager f-string assert message (self.assertTrue(line, f'...{proc.stderr.read()}')) evaluated proc.stderr.read() UNCONDITIONALLY even on the success path, deadlocking because the child's stderr pipe never hit EOF while still running -- confirmed via faulthandler.dump_traceback_later pinpointing the exact blocked line, fixed by moving the stderr read inside an explicit 'if not line' branch. Also fixed a session-id mismatch in the refusal-comparison test. Full suite already run and attested at c2: 6 failed (exactly the pinned red set, unchanged) / 2157 passed / 1061 subtests.
